item.title: Participation de l’Institut à la Journée de politique extérieure de l’Assemblée fédérale
item.description: Grâce à la collaboration des services du Parlement avec le Centre Albert Hirschman sur la démocratie, l’Institut a participé à la Journée de politique extérieure de l’Assemblée fédérale le 28 octobre, sur le thème “Le multilatéralisme sous pression : les réponses de l’Europe, entre sécurité et démocratie”. Marie-Laure Salles , directrice, Achim Wennmann , directeur des partenariats stratégiques, et Christine Lutringer , directrice exécutive du Centre Albert Hirschman sur la démocratie, ont représenté l’Institut.

item.title: Why young protesters in France are turning against TV channel CNews
item.description: What happens when a protest movement turns against the media covering it? In France, students are challenging the government’s education policies and increasingly the news outlets through which their demands reach the public. Drawing from her research on “asymmetric visibility”, Dr Laura Bullon-Cassis , a Research Fellow at the Albert Hirschman Centre on Democracy, shares her insights in this article published by The Conversation .

item.title: Revitalizing International Support for Democratic Renewal
item.description: How can international cooperation become more inclusive, participatory, and democratically accountable, at a time when multilateral institutions face growing challenges?

item.title: Brazilians Have Voted: What Is Next?
item.description: In a lunch briefing organised in collaboration with the Albert Hirschman Centre on Democracy, Professor Graziella Moraes Silva addressed the results of the second round of Brazil’s presidential elections, which secured the reelection of President Lula. She analysed the choices made by Brazilian voters, considering what they reveal about the country's political and social dynamics.

item.title: EXPLORING THE CO-CREATION PROCESS OF THE EXHIBIT “WHAT IS THE FUTURE?”
item.description: As part of the Democracy Week programme, the Geneva Graduate Institute community was offered a guided tour of the new exhibit “What is the Future”? The exhibit was co-created by groups of young schoolchildren and highlighted varying perspectives on time, the future and its representations.

item.title: UNDERSTANDING AND ADDRESSING AFFECTIVE POLARISATION
item.description: Yanina Welp and her colleagues present their research findings and outline a diagnostic matrix for assessing polarisation.

item.title: IA, désinformation et éducation : quels défis pour la démocratie ?
Médias : quelle confiance à l’ère de l’intelligence artificielle ?
item.description: Un débat public co-organisé avec la Ville de Genève a analysé les adaptations du paysage médiatique face à l’IA et la désinformation.

item.title: THE US AT THE POLLS: THE 2026 MIDTERMS AND THE FUTURE OF DEMOCRACY
item.description: A Democracy Week webinar brought together speakers from across the political spectrum to examine what the US midterms reveal about the future of American democracy.

item.title: Exploring Geneva’s democratic ecosystem: from philanthropy to international cooperation
item.description: To kick off Democracy Week, a group of 70 people joined the immersive tour "Explorer Geneve: Democratie, Philanthropie Et Institutions Internationales" to explore democracy beyond the ballot box, through philanthropy, civil society, media, research and international cooperation. Proving that democracy is about institutions and participation, but above all, it is about people.

item.title: Direct Democracy: A Response to Democratic Challenges in France and Around the World?
item.description: On the International Day of Democracy, a panel comprising experts on Swiss direct democracy took the stage at Rousseau’s birth home and discussed to what extent the institution could be introduced as a means to combat global democratic backsliding

item.title: Dan Hicks Explores the Politics of Museums and Monumentality at the Geneva Graduate Institute
item.description: Geneva, 17 September 2026 - The Centre for Digital Humanities and Multilateralism (CDHM) welcomed renowned archaeologist, anthropologist and museum curator Dan Hicks for a seminar devoted to his latest book, Every Monument Will Fall: A Story of Remembering and Forgetting . Organised in collaboration with the Albert Hirschman Centre on Democracy and the Department of Anthropology and Sociology, the event brought together researchers, students and members of the public to discuss the politics of monuments, museums and collective memory.

item.title: Democracy Week 2026 Round-up
item.description: Throughout Geneva Democracy Week, as every year, the Albert Hirschman Centre on Democracy brought together researchers, policymakers, civil society representatives, students and the wider public to explore contemporary challenges to democracy through discussions, workshops and interactive experiences.

item.title: NEW SNSF AMBIZIONE GRANT FOR Laura Bullon-Cassis
item.description: Laura Bullón-Cassis will examine the growing role of private technology companies in Earth observation and what this shift means for how climate change is seen, known and governed.

item.title: YOUTH CLIMATE ACTIVISM: WHAT'S LEFT?
item.description: The Albert Hirschman launches a new podcast mini-series on the future of climate politics, democracy and social justice in Europe.
